"PROJECT: DEAD WORLD — 3D MOBILE SURVIVAL

1. CORE VISION

Create a complete, highly detailed, 3D open-world zombie survival game for Android mobile devices.

The game must deliver a deep, realistic, systemic survival experience inspired by hardcore zombie survival simulations such as Project Zomboid.

This must NOT be a simple zombie shooter, linear campaign, arcade survival game, or basic prototype.

The main focus is survival, exploration, resource management, realism, environmental interaction, emergent gameplay, and player freedom.

The world must feel alive, dangerous, abandoned, and persistent.

Create an original game with its own assets, locations, interface, characters, and world design.

2. CAMERA AND GRAPHICS

- Fully 3D environments.
- Detailed character models.
- Realistic environmental lighting.
- Dynamic shadows.
- Atmospheric fog.
- Realistic vegetation.
- Destructible environmental objects where supported.
- High-quality textures with mobile optimization.
- Dynamic weather.
- Day and night cycles.
- Realistic animations.
- Smooth camera movement.
- Isometric or elevated third-person camera.
- Camera rotation and zoom.
- Mobile graphics settings: Low, Medium, High and Ultra.

The game must prioritize stable performance on Android devices.

3. OPEN WORLD

Create a large, explorable, persistent world.

Include:

- Residential neighborhoods.
- Downtown districts.
- Gas stations.
- Supermarkets.
- Hospitals.
- Police stations.
- Fire stations.
- Warehouses.
- Industrial zones.
- Farms.
- Forests.
- Highways.
- Parking lots.
- Small rural settlements.
- Abandoned commercial buildings.

Every building should have interiors when technically possible.

Buildings must contain furniture, containers, doors, windows, loot, and environmental storytelling.

The world must be explorable without forced linear progression.

4. PLAYER CHARACTER

Implement a complete character system.

Character attributes:

- Health.
- Hunger.
- Thirst.
- Fatigue.
- Sleepiness.
- Body temperature.
- Stress.
- Panic.
- Physical fitness.
- Strength.
- Endurance.
- Carrying capacity.

Include:

- Walking.
- Running.
- Sprinting.
- Crouching.
- Sneaking.
- Jumping over obstacles.
- Climbing supported obstacles.
- Opening and closing doors.
- Window interaction.
- Searching containers.
- Picking up objects.
- Dropping objects.
- Equipping weapons.
- Using tools.
- Eating.
- Drinking.
- Sleeping.

All actions must have appropriate animations and contextual interactions.

5. ZOMBIE AI

Create zombies with independent AI behavior.

Zombies must:

- Wander through the environment.
- React to sounds.
- Investigate suspicious noises.
- Detect visible players.
- Chase detected targets.
- Lose track of players.
- Search nearby areas.
- React to environmental disturbances.
- Attack doors and windows.
- Break through barricades when possible.
- Gather around noises.
- Follow groups of zombies.
- Become more dangerous in dense urban areas.

Include different zombie conditions:

- Slow zombies.
- Fast zombies.
- Weak zombies.
- Strong zombies.
- Recently infected zombies.
- Decomposed zombies.

Zombie AI must be optimized for mobile performance.

Use distance-based simulation and efficient AI updates.

6. COMBAT SYSTEM

Implement realistic melee combat.

Weapons:

- Kitchen knives.
- Baseball bats.
- Metal pipes.
- Hammers.
- Axes.
- Crowbars.
- Improvised weapons.

Implement:

- Attack animations.
- Hit detection.
- Weapon durability.
- Stamina consumption.
- Attack cooldowns.
- Knockback.
- Enemy reactions.
- Weapon condition.
- Contextual combat interactions.

Include firearms as a later system with ammunition management, sound propagation, recoil, and weapon maintenance.

Combat must be dangerous and resource-intensive.

7. INVENTORY SYSTEM

Create a detailed inventory interface.

Features:

- Item grid.
- Item categories.
- Item descriptions.
- Item weight.
- Item condition.
- Stackable resources.
- Equipment slots.
- Backpacks.
- Containers.
- Looting interface.
- Drag-and-drop where supported.
- Quick access slots.

Include different container types:

- Backpacks.
- School bags.
- Boxes.
- Cabinets.
- Refrigerators.
- Vehicle trunks.
- Storage crates.

Every item must have meaningful gameplay functionality.

8. SURVIVAL SYSTEM

Implement a complete survival simulation.

Hunger:

- Hunger increases over time.
- Different foods provide different nutritional values.
- Food can spoil.
- Eating reduces hunger.

Thirst:

- Water is essential.
- Different containers store different amounts.
- Drinking reduces thirst.
- Water sources can become unavailable.

Fatigue:

- Physical activity consumes energy.
- Running consumes more stamina.
- Rest restores stamina.

Sleep:

- The character becomes exhausted.
- Sleeping restores energy.
- Sleeping must advance world time.
- Unsafe sleeping locations must create risks.

Temperature:

- Weather affects body temperature.
- Clothing influences insulation.
- Rain and cold affect comfort.

Health:

- Injuries.
- Bleeding.
- Infection.
- Pain.
- Bandages.
- Medical supplies.
- Recovery over time.

9. LOOT AND RESOURCE SYSTEM

Create a contextual loot-generation system.

Examples:

- Supermarkets contain food and household supplies.
- Hospitals contain medical supplies.
- Police stations contain law-enforcement equipment.
- Hardware stores contain construction tools.
- Gas stations contain fuel and convenience goods.
- Residential buildings contain domestic objects.

Loot must be randomized but logically distributed.

Items must have rarity and usefulness.

10. BUILDING AND BASE SYSTEM

Allow players to establish safehouses.

Implement:

- Furniture placement.
- Storage.
- Barricades.
- Doors.
- Windows.
- Walls.
- Defensive structures.
- Resource storage.
- Building repairs.
- Object relocation.

Allow players to transform abandoned buildings into survival bases.

11. VEHICLE SYSTEM

Implement functional vehicles.

Vehicle categories:

- Sedans.
- Pickup trucks.
- Vans.
- SUVs.
- Utility vehicles.

Features:

- Enter and exit vehicles.
- Driving physics.
- Steering.
- Acceleration.
- Braking.
- Fuel consumption.
- Engine condition.
- Vehicle damage.
- Storage capacity.
- Locked vehicles.
- Vehicle keys.
- Battery condition.

Vehicles must be useful for transportation and supply collection.

12. ENVIRONMENT AND WEATHER

Implement:

- Dynamic sunlight.
- Rain.
- Storms.
- Fog.
- Wind.
- Cloud coverage.
- Temperature changes.
- Seasonal environmental variation.

Environmental sounds must include:

- Wind.
- Rain.
- Thunder.
- Birds.
- Insects.
- Distant alarms.
- Breaking glass.
- Footsteps.
- Zombie vocalizations.

Sound must contribute to immersion and gameplay.

13. WORLD TIME

Create a persistent simulation clock.

- Full day and night cycles.
- Time-dependent lighting.
- Sleep advances time.
- World events can occur over time.
- Food continues to spoil.
- Zombies continue their simulation.
- Weather changes over time.

14. MOBILE USER INTERFACE

The game must be designed specifically for touchscreen devices.

Include:

- Virtual movement joystick.
- Camera control.
- Contextual interaction button.
- Attack button.
- Sprint button.
- Crouch button.
- Inventory button.
- Map button.
- Equipment shortcuts.

The interface must be customizable.

Support different screen resolutions and aspect ratios.

Avoid overcrowded controls.

15. MAP AND NAVIGATION

Create a detailed interactive map.

Features:

- Current player position.
- Discovered buildings.
- Roads.
- Neighborhoods.
- Custom markers.
- Explored areas.
- Undiscovered areas.

The map should gradually reveal information as the player explores.

16. SAVE SYSTEM

Implement persistent local saves.

Save:

- Player position.
- Player inventory.
- Character attributes.
- Building states.
- Loot states.
- Zombie states.
- Vehicle positions.
- World time.
- Weather.
- Base construction.

The player must be able to close the game and continue later without losing progress.

17. GAMEPLAY DIFFICULTY

Provide customizable difficulty settings.

- Zombie population.
- Zombie awareness.
- Loot abundance.
- Resource scarcity.
- Survival difficulty.
- Day length.
- Starting equipment.

Include a sandbox mode.

18. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

This is an Android-first project.

Prioritize:

- Stable frame rate.
- Efficient memory usage.
- Optimized 3D assets.
- Object pooling.
- Level-of-detail systems.
- Distance-based AI simulation.
- Efficient collision detection.
- Asynchronous loading where supported.
- Mobile-friendly rendering.
- Persistent save architecture.

Avoid unnecessary background calculations.

19. DEVELOPMENT PRIORITIES

Do not create a static visual demo.

The result must be a playable game.

Prioritize functional systems over decorative features.

Development order:

1. Player movement and camera.
2. Basic 3D world.
3. Character interactions.
4. Inventory.
5. Zombie AI.
6. Combat.
7. Loot generation.
8. Survival mechanics.
9. Building interiors.
10. Save system.
11. Vehicles.
12. Base construction.
13. Weather and advanced world simulation.

If a feature cannot be fully implemented, create a functional simplified version rather than a decorative placeholder.

20. FINAL OBJECTIVE

Deliver a playable, immersive, persistent 3D mobile zombie survival game.

The experience must emphasize freedom, realism, exploration, tension, resource management, and emergent survival stories.

Every system must interact with other systems whenever technically possible.

The final result must be a functional game project with organized source code, assets, and clear project structure.

Do not stop after creating the main menu or a visual prototype.

Build the actual playable experience.
